description.narrative: The European Union (EU) offer to address the region¿s vulnerability to disasters ¿ one of the most pressing challenges facing the Caribbean, of which the EU itself is an integral part ¿ sends a strong political signal. This approach is strategic in a geopolitical landscape increasingly dominated by power politics, where visible, reliable and long-term engagement matters, and featured prominently in President Von der Leyen¿s participation at the CARICOM Summit in 2025. Subsequently, this commitment was formalised by Von der Leyen to the region through exchange of letter with PM Mottley. Hurricane Melissa exposed both the scale of vulnerability of the Caribbean and the strategic value of a coordinated Team Europe response. This experience underscored the need to structurally integrate European public and private capacities across preparedness, response and early recovery capacity in the region. This effectively complements the mandate of humanitarian actors, including ECHO, on anticipatory actions and first response. The proposed StormReady programme responds directly to this commitment, investing in logistical systems structured around private-sector response solutions to disasters. It complements the recently launched StormWatch, which enhances the Caribbean capacity to forecast and monitor extreme weather events through EU digital and satellite technology, services and expertise.StormReady expands the EU¿s disaster response logistics systems through European naval, air and commercial capabilities and by establishing a stand-by network of EU companies integrated into regional disaster response and early recovery arrangements. This will equip the INTPA Regional Hub with concrete tools to consolidate the EU¿s added value on Disaster Risk Management (DRM)across CARICOM and non-CARICOM countries, EU OCTs and French Overseas Departments.
